title: The Lantern Road
logline: Climbing to light the road home, a girl turns back to relight the lanterns the wind put out, and finds who was lost in the dark.
look: Painterly storybook dusk: violet sky, indigo hills, a winding road of paper lanterns glowing amber; gentle paint boil; stars mirror the lanterns at the end.
narrator: female, middle-aged, moderate pitch, british accent
A gentle mother reading aloud at bedtime
music: Harp and flute lullaby; wind noise rises with a low clarinet; strings bloom when the two lights meet.

shots.direction: EWS 24mm · slow push · fade in — a dusk valley; a winding road of unlit lanterns climbs a hill
MS 50mm · locked · cut — a girl with a lantern leaves a cottage; her mother waves from the door
WS 35mm · tracking · cut — she walks uphill, lighting each roadside lantern from her flame
CU 85mm · hold · cut — a gust; her flame shivers
WS 35mm · locked · cut — behind her, the lanterns blow out one by one
CU 85mm · push in · cut — she shields her flame with both hands; it holds
WS 24mm low angle · tracking · cut — she turns and walks back down, relighting every lantern behind her
EWS 24mm · locked · dissolve — night; the road glows again; far below a small dark figure climbs toward her
MS 50mm · slow push · cut — they meet: her grandfather, his lantern dead; she lights it from hers
WS 35mm · tracking · cut — two lights walk up the hill together
EWS 24mm · crane up · dissolve — the whole road lit like a necklace of stars beneath the real stars
MS 50mm · locked · fade out — at the cottage door, grandfather hangs his lantern; the door closes on warm light

narration.text: Every evening, someone had to light the road.
But the wind does not care whose turn it is.
She could have kept climbing. She went back instead.
Because a light behind you is a road for someone else.
